cases.description: Microsoft's example: five cash flows at irregular dates
A date before the first is #NUM!
Values and dates of different counts are #NUM!

Dates where a correctly rounded power and e^(x ln(1+rate)), the ^ operator's, differ in the last place: Excel's double is what e^(x ln(1+rate)) summed from the first value gives, where Math.Pow summed so is 8 units in the last place away; a correctly rounded power gives it only summed otherwise (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, Search.cs)
Whole years apart: 1+rate raised by squaring, as PV and FV raise it to a whole number, gives Excel's double (Math.Pow gives it too here), where e^(x ln(1+rate)) gives 2023.0065393622895
Whole years apart: squaring gives Excel's double, where e^(x ln(1+rate)) and Math.Pow give 2277.5848519247415
A rate of -1: #NUM!
A rate of -1 with every date the first: #NUM!, where Math.Pow, which the engine took before, gave -7250 (0 to the power 0 is 1)
A rate below -1 with the dates whole years apart: #NUM!, where squaring and Math.Pow give 400
A rate of -2: #NUM!
101 days: the days divided by 365, where the days multiplied by 1/365 give -7286.877809009439
A rate of -0.5, above -1: #NUM!, as XNPV-017's; Excel answered no rate below 0 it was asked

Values in no order of their dates: each discount e^(x ln(1+rate)) with the exponential correctly rounded. At 797 days the platform's (glibc's) exp gives 1.2313555711418422, one unit in the last place below the correctly rounded 1.2313555711418425, and the sum 700.2269770028581, 4 units away (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, Search.cs)

Values in no order of their dates, chosen to tell the evaluations that give XNPV-001 and 004 apart (discriminate-xnpv.txt): the days over 365, squaring at whole years and e^(x ln(1+rate)) otherwise, each value divided and summed in the order given
As XNPV-014, with seven values: Excel's double is that evaluation's
An input chosen to tell the evaluations that give XNPV-001 and 004 apart (discriminate-xnpv.txt): Excel's double is the engine's
A rate of -0.5: #NUM!, as XNPV-012's

Where the last addition nearly cancels: the sum from the first value, 1.1368683772161603E-13 (run 18a), where Excel's last-addition adjustment (as a Formula's last addition, and SUM's, is adjusted) gives 0; it tells XNPV's two evaluations apart (Search.cs)
A rate of 0: #NUM! (run 18a): XNPV's check of the rate is "0 or below", where "below 0" would answer the sum of the values, 3000

A small negative rate: #NUM!, the check of the rate Excel gave at every negative rate it was asked, -0.01 among them (run 18a), and which none of the evaluations that give XNPV's observed doubles gives
An Error Value among the values at a rate below 0: #NUM! (run 18a), the rate checked before the values are read, where the values read first give #N/A

Text among the values at a rate below 0: #NUM! (run 18a), the rate checked before the values are read; what Excel gives for text alone has not been observed, and the engine refuses it where an order of XNPV's checks reaches it first
An Error Value among the values at a rate of 0: #NUM! (run 18a), "0 or below" checked before the values are read, where "below 0", or the values read first, give #N/A
An Error Value among the values beside counts that differ: #NUM! (run 18a), the counts checked before the values are read, as at XNPV-003, where the values read first give #N/A

An Error Value among the values beside a later date before the first: #N/A (run 18a), the values read before a date before the first is checked, where the dates checked first give #NUM!, as at XNPV-002

An Error Value first among the values and another first among the dates: the date's, #DIV/0! (run 18a), the dates read before the values, or each date before its value, where the values read first give #N/A
A rate that is an Error Value beside an Error Value among the values: the rate's, #DIV/0! (run 18a), where the values read first give #N/A
A rate that is an Error Value beside counts that differ: the rate's, #DIV/0! (run 18a), where the counts checked first give #NUM!, as at XNPV-003

An Error Value among the dates, and a date before the first after it: #N/A (run 18a), the dates read in order and the first failure answered, where a check of every date against the first made before the dates' Error Values gives #NUM!, as at XNPV-002
Two different Error Values among the values: #N/A (run 18a), the values read from the first, where any other order gives #DIV/0!
